justification: The original partial attribution remains the best fit, but the new deployment evidence materially weakens the robustness claim. The prior evidence showed acceptable performance under several predefined perturbations, formatting variation, OCR degradation, and limited out-of-distribution testing, which supported some robustness beyond nominal conditions. However, the newly observed second-hospital templates were not represented in the validation corpus, yet they fall within the intended deployment categories; on these documents, accuracy dropped to 72.6%, and the out-of-distribution mechanism flagged only 31.2%. This shows that the system's behavior is not robust across at least one relevant real-world deployment condition within scope. The earlier evidence still supports some robustness under tested conditions, but the added information reveals a significant untested/underperforming template variation, so the attribution should be weakened rather than strengthened or fully supported.
evidence_affected: A second hospital began using document templates that were not represented in the original validation corpus.
These templates fall within the deployment categories specified for the system.
Accuracy for 4,830 documents using these templates was 72.6%.
The out-of-distribution mechanism flagged 31.2% of these documents.
No other measured deployment category showed a comparable change during the same period.
With 10% randomly removed non-critical fields, accuracy was 93.7%.
With the predefined OCR degradation transformation, accuracy was 92.1%.
Across the predefined formatting-variation set, accuracy ranged from 91.6% to 94.8%.
The validation protocol contains three predefined perturbation tests; corresponding accuracies were 92.8%, 90.9%, and 93.4%.
Of the 1,200 out-of-distribution samples, 1,127 were flagged by the out-of-distribution mechanism.
